messages:
jen-support: FYI: Acme reporting huge tail latency and a spike in EU billing for traffic that should be us-west. They claim client sets region=us-west. urgent.
leo-customer: we send region via both query param and header. example: `GET /v1/generate?region=us-west` plus `X-Client-Region: us-west`. still seeing EU endpoints.
jen-support: asked for raw capture, they provided proxied request from their ALB. snippet below.
leo-customer: ```
GET /v1/generate?region=us-west HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Client-Region: us-west
X-Region: "null"
User-Agent: AcmeBot/1.2
```
jen-support: note: X-Region contains the string "null" (literal) and sometimes empty `X-Region:` with no value depending on ALB behaviour.
chris-runtime: :eyes: that could be it. router header precedence treats any present header as authoritative, even empty or literal-null string. empty wins over query param -> fallback routing to default (EU).
maria-sre: can you paste router log for this request id?
jen-support: here's redacted router trace from 2024-10-12 14:03:21 (request id r-9a1b):
```
router TRACE r-9a1b: incoming headers: {X-Region: "", X-Client-Region: "us-west"} 
router INFO r-9a1b: header X-Region present -> apply precedence -> route.region = parseHeader("") -> returns null-region -> select fallback region eu-west-1
router DEBUG r-9a1b: selected model pool: eu-pool-5, latency expected 220ms
```
chris-runtime: yep. bug: parseHeader treats empty string as "explicit but empty" and still marks header as set. precedence logic uses header existence not value non-emptiness.
ben-support: customer also saw billing at EU pricing for that day. billing team says meter tags come from selected region at routing time. need audit and possible credit.
sam-platform: immediate mitigation: we can update router to strip headers equal to empty string or common placeholders ("null", "NULL", "<null>") before precedence check. low-risk patch. can roll as feature flag.
maria-sre: ops note: this explains latency increase too — requests hit EU pools and crossed region network. will cause increased p95.
chris-runtime: repro steps I used locally:
```bash
# simulating ALB sending an empty header
curl -v -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west' -H 'X-Region:' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-west'
```
observed router chooses eu. attaching server-side trace.
jen-support: customer on call now; asked for ETA and rollback plan.
sam-platform: propose two-step: 1) hotfix to treat empty/placeholder header as absent (rollback safe) behind flag, 2) run a backfill job to reclassify billing tags for affected request ids.
ben-support: please capture list of affected request ids and date ranges (Acme only for now). billing will prepare credits once we confirm.
chris-runtime: I'll open a PR with unit tests for header parsing and add a flag gate. assign to me.
jen-support: @chris-runtime please set patch to roll into canary region first and notify customer.
chris-runtime: will do. deploying to canary in ~30m. deploy-bot: deploy started for canary/router-fix by chris-runtime
deploy-bot: canary deploy success (router-fix v2024.10.12-rc3)
jen-support: customer reported initial requests now hitting US pools after canary. :thumbsup:
ben-support: collect invoice impact and pending credits. I'll coordinate with finance.
maria-sre: follow-up items: add observability alert for header-value anomalies (empty/null/placeholder) and a dashboard showing precedence decisions per request.
sam-platform: also recommend doc update for SDKs: prefer query param or explicit header semantics; call out that empty headers can be injected by proxies.
leo-customer: thank you all. shipping a quick ALB fix on our side too to stop sending empty X-Region. appreciate the fast turnaround.
jen-support: leaving this thread open until billing resolved and postmortem drafted. will update status here.
